name: assistanthub-docs
description: Retrieval benchmark over a frozen snapshot (2026-09-24) of AssistantHub's own documentation: README, REST/MCP API references, chat data flow, telemetry, testing, changelog, Docker links, and nine archived design notes. 120 questions spanning paraphrase, lexical, multi-document, deep-detail, table, metadata-filter, follow-up and unanswerable cases.

documents.title: AssistantHub README
documents.summary: Product overview, release highlights, Docker quick start, configuration, API overview, MCP server, architecture and SDKs.

documents.title: AssistantHub REST API Reference
documents.summary: Full REST API reference with request/response schemas, settings fields and error codes.

documents.title: AssistantHub MCP API Reference
documents.summary: MCP server transports, configuration, tool naming, secret handling and REST route coverage matrix.

documents.title: AssistantHub Chat Data Flow
documents.summary: Current public assistant chat path: validation, retrieval, utility LLM steps, inference and persistence.

documents.title: AssistantHub Telemetry
documents.summary: OpenTelemetry metrics, traces and logs, configuration, bundled observability stack and integration notes.

documents.title: Running Tests
documents.summary: Test projects, runners, environment variables, SDK tests and crawler validation checklist.

documents.title: AssistantHub Changelog
documents.summary: Release notes from v0.2.0 through v0.16.0 and unreleased changes.

documents.title: Using Claude or Cursor with AssistantHub MCP
documents.summary: Step-by-step setup of the AssistantHub MCP server for Claude Code and Cursor.

documents.title: AssistantHub Docker Links and Default Credentials
documents.summary: Local Docker dashboard and backend URLs plus default credentials for every service.

documents.title: Crawlers Implementation Plan
documents.summary: Archived implementation plan for native web crawlers, crawl plans and operations.

documents.title: Partio v0.4.0 Summarization Integration Plan
documents.summary: Archived plan for integrating Partio summarization and endpoint management.

documents.summary: Archived plan for per-assistant Slack Socket Mode integration.

queries.text: How long does AssistantHub keep conversation logs before deleting them automatically, and how often does that purge run?
evidence: RetentionDays int 7 Number of days to retain chat history records
Records older than this are automatically deleted by the background cleanup service (runs every hour)
Retention period in days for chat history records (0 = keep indefinitely). Background cleanup runs hourly.
queries.answer: Chat history is kept 7 days by default (0 keeps it forever); the cleanup job runs every hour.

queries.text: Is there a way to have the bot skip searching documents when a follow-up can be answered from what was already said in the conversation?
evidence: Optional LLM-based retrieval gate that intelligently decides whether each user message requires a new document search or can be answered from existing conversation context, reducing unnecessary retrieval calls.
an LLM call classifies whether each user message requires new document retrieval (RETRIEVE) or can be answered from existing conversation context (SKIP)
queries.answer: Yes. Enable the LLM-based retrieval gate (EnableRetrievalGate), which decides per message whether to RETRIEVE or SKIP.

queries.text: What happens to earlier messages when a chat gets so long it would overflow the model?
evidence: Automatic summarization of older messages when the conversation approaches the context window limit, preserving continuity across long conversations.
When the conversation history approaches the context window limit, older messages are automatically summarized (compacted).
queries.answer: Older messages are automatically summarized (compacted) before the final inference call.

queries.text: If the LLM step that re-scores search hits crashes or returns garbage, does the user's chat request fail?
evidence: If the re-ranking LLM call fails or returns unparseable output, the pipeline falls back to the original retrieval ordering. Re-ranking never blocks chat completion.
queries.answer: No. It falls back to the original retrieval ordering; re-ranking never blocks the chat.

queries.text: Why does the relevance-scoring step put every candidate passage into one prompt instead of making a call per passage?
evidence: all candidate chunks are presented in a single prompt with indexed labels
This keeps latency proportional to one LLM call, not N.
queries.answer: To keep latency at a single LLM call instead of one call per chunk.

queries.text: When I remove a file from the knowledge base, what else gets cleaned up along with it?
evidence: Delete a document, its S3 object, all associated RecallDB embeddings, and its Verbex text-search record.
Document deletion now also removes associated Verbex text-search records
queries.answer: Its S3 object, all of its RecallDB embeddings, and its Verbex text-search record.

queries.text: Does leaving the metrics instrumentation in the code slow anything down when nothing is collecting it?
evidence: Emitting is a near-free no-op until a host subscribes, so there is no cost when telemetry is disabled.
queries.answer: No. Emitting is a near-free no-op until a telemetry host subscribes.

queries.text: Why can't I break down the Prometheus metrics by tenant or by document?
evidence: High-cardinality identifiers (tenant id, document id, request id) are attached to spans, never to metrics.
queries.answer: Those high-cardinality IDs are only attached to trace spans, never to metric labels.

queries.text: My crawler runs in the AssistantHub container but the SMB share lives on my own machine at localhost. How does that get resolved?
evidence: localhost from inside assistanthub-server means the container, not the host machine
AssistantHub normalizes loopback file-server hostnames to that alias when it is available
loopback file-server hostnames such as localhost, 127.0.0.1, and ::1 are treated as the Docker host
queries.answer: Loopback hostnames are mapped to host.docker.internal (the Docker host) when that alias resolves.

queries.text: Will the Slack bot answer in the main channel, or keep its replies grouped under the message that asked?
evidence: Slack responses are posted back into the originating Slack thread
replies are posted back into the originating Slack thread
queries.answer: Replies are posted in the originating Slack thread.

queries.text: Are the Slack app and bot tokens encrypted when AssistantHub saves them?
evidence: Slack tokens are stored in the AssistantHub database in plaintext, so rely on your deployment's at-rest protections
queries.answer: No. They are stored in plaintext; rely on the deployment's at-rest protections.

queries.text: Can people using the public chat page switch on extra model tools such as web search themselves?
evidence: Public chat users cannot choose or broaden tool permissions.
queries.answer: No. Tool permissions come from the admin-configured assistant tool policy.

queries.text: What's the point of also pulling in the passages right before and after a search hit?
evidence: This provides surrounding context for each match, which is critical for RAG pipelines where isolated chunks lose meaning without their adjacent content.
Provides surrounding document context for each search match.
queries.answer: It gives the model the surrounding document context so isolated chunks don't lose their meaning.

queries.text: If I turn on adjacent-chunk expansion, will answers end up listing more sources?
evidence: Does not affect scoring, citation count, or top-K limits.
Neighbor content enriches the context block but does not create additional citations.
queries.answer: No. Each matched chunk still maps to one citation source.

queries.text: If I pin a few files to a chat message, can the model read their raw storage objects or summarize them in full?
evidence: Attached documents narrow retrieval scope. They do not request whole-document summarization and do not grant object-storage access.
attached_document_ids narrows retrieval scope only; it does not grant direct object storage access.
queries.answer: No. Attached documents only narrow retrieval to those documents.

queries.text: After wiping everything and starting the stack again, why does the main API container sit waiting before it starts?
evidence: assistanthub-server will not start until partio-server is healthy
assistanthub-server waits for partio-server to report healthy before starting
queries.answer: It intentionally waits for partio-server (and postgres-init) to be healthy before starting.

queries.text: If a user drags a file from their laptop into the chat, does it become part of the assistant's permanent knowledge base?
evidence: These files are not added to the assistant collection.
without adding those files to the assistant collection
queries.answer: No. Local attachments are text-extracted for that request's prompt only and are not stored in the collection.

queries.text: How does a scheduled crawl figure out whether a file it saw last time has been modified?
evidence: compares two enumerations to produce Added, Changed, Deleted, and Unchanged lists
Compare in precedence order — first mismatch means Changed
queries.answer: It compares against the previous enumeration: ContentLength, then ETag, SHA256/SHA1/MD5 hashes and LastModifiedUtc; the first mismatch marks it Changed.

queries.text: If a file failed to ingest during one crawl, will the next crawl try it again?
evidence: This ensures failed items get another ingestion attempt on the next crawl.
queries.answer: Yes. Previously failed items are re-added to the Added list on the next crawl.

queries.text: Why were model endpoints kept shared across tenants instead of giving each tenant its own?
evidence: Keep endpoints global (configured by global admin), any tenant can use them
more isolation but more management overhead
queries.answer: Per-tenant endpoints add management overhead, so endpoints stay global, managed by the global admin.

queries.text: Could a burst of uploads make documents fail because the embedding service is overloaded?
evidence: so bursts that trip Partio v0.5.0's per-endpoint concurrency/queue limits no longer fail documents outright
Ingestion automatically retries transient Partio failures (408/429/502/503/504) with exponential backoff so bursts do not fail documents.
queries.answer: Not anymore. Ingestion retries transient Partio failures with exponential backoff (Chunking.MaxRetries, default 3).

queries.text: Can I watch an evaluation run's progress live instead of polling for results?
evidence: Stream evaluation run progress via Server-Sent Events (SSE). Events are sent as each fact is evaluated.
queries.answer: Yes, via the SSE stream at GET /v1.0/eval/runs/{runId}/stream.

queries.text: Does turning on source references in answers cost an extra model call per turn?
evidence: Citations are model-generated via prompt instruction and extracted via regex; no extra LLM calls.
queries.answer: No. Citations come from prompt instructions and regex extraction; there are no extra LLM calls.

queries.text: What happens if the model points to a source number that isn't in the list it was given?
evidence: Invalid references (e.g., 99 when only 3 sources exist) are silently dropped
queries.answer: The invalid reference is silently dropped from referenced_indices.

queries.text: Why isn't the Slack-formatted version of a reply what gets saved in conversation history?
evidence: This prevents compaction, replay, and cross-transport history from ingesting Slack-specific formatting.
Slack responses are transport-shaped only at delivery time while canonical response text is persisted to history
queries.answer: Only canonical response text is persisted, so compaction, replay and other transports never see Slack-specific formatting.

queries.text: What does ASSISTANTHUB_TEST_KEEP_ARTIFACTS do?
evidence: Preserve spawned server/MCP temp directories, logs, and databases for inspection when set to 1, true, or yes.
queries.answer: When set to 1/true/yes it keeps the spawned server/MCP temp directories, logs and databases for inspection.

queries.text: What is the default MaxQueueDepth on a Partio endpoint and what happens when it is 0?
evidence: 0 rejects excess requests immediately with 429 Too Many Requests
0 (the default) keeps today's behavior -- requests over the concurrency limit are rejected immediately with 429
queries.answer: Default is 0: requests over the concurrency limit are rejected immediately with 429.

queries.text: What does POST /v1.0/crawlplans/connectivity (without a plan id) do?
evidence: Test connectivity for a draft crawl plan payload without creating or updating a persisted crawl plan.
queries.answer: Tests connectivity for an unsaved (draft) crawl plan payload without persisting it.

queries.text: What does RecallDb.SupportsMultiDocumentFilter control?
evidence: AssistantHub then loops over single-document DocumentId searches for attached-document retrieval and logs a fallback warning.
set it to false only for RecallDB deployments that do not accept native DocumentIds search filters
queries.answer: Defaults to true; set false for RecallDB versions without native DocumentIds filters, making AssistantHub loop over single-document searches with a warning.

queries.text: What does the migrations/010_upgrade_to_v0.12.0 provider script add?
evidence: Existing deployments can add the new telemetry columns and chat_history_performance_events table
queries.answer: The v0.12.0 telemetry columns and the chat_history_performance_events table.

queries.text: What is ASSISTANTHUB_OTLP_ENDPOINT used for?
evidence: Set ASSISTANTHUB_OTLP_ENDPOINT (and ASSISTANTHUB_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true) to your OpenTelemetry Collector or any OTLP-compatible endpoint.
queries.answer: It overrides Telemetry.OtlpEndpoint, the OTLP collector endpoint telemetry is exported to.

queries.text: What does the object_byte_limit tool error mean?
evidence: Aggregate model-visible S3 object byte cap per assistant chat turn. Exceeding the cap returns a structured object_byte_limit tool error instead of source text.
queries.answer: The turn exceeded MaxObjectBytesPerTurn, the per-turn cap on model-visible S3 object bytes (default 524288).

queries.text: Which ErrorCodes can POST /v1.0/assistants/{assistantId}/settings/tools/validate return?
evidence: Current validation codes are invalid_tool_policy_json, unknown_allowed_tool, no_tool_enabled, and no_available_tools.
queries.answer: invalid_tool_policy_json, unknown_allowed_tool, no_tool_enabled and no_available_tools.

queries.text: What is the assistanthub:tool-calling label on a Partio completion endpoint?
evidence: AssistantHub persists these capability fields in Partio endpoint metadata using the reserved label assistanthub:tool-calling and reserved tags
queries.answer: A reserved label AssistantHub uses to persist tool-calling capability on the Partio endpoint.

queries.text: What is the default value of Storage.MaxInlineBinaryBytes?
evidence: default inline size limit is 5242880 bytes
queries.answer: 5242880 bytes (5 MiB).

queries.text: What does the --include-models flag do for the factory reset script?
evidence: Downloaded Ollama models are kept by default; pass --include-models to remove them as well.
queries.answer: It also removes downloaded Ollama models, which are otherwise kept.

queries.text: What is EnableServerGeneratedQueryVariants?
evidence: Allows the server to add deterministic collection-search query variants, such as punctuation-normalized forms, after model-supplied queries and only within MaxSearchQueriesPerCall.
queries.answer: An opt-in tool-policy flag (default false) letting the server add deterministic query variants within MaxSearchQueriesPerCall.

queries.text: What does GET /v1.0/configuration/external-search/status return?
evidence: Retrieve a safe external-search configuration status summary for admin UI and diagnostics. The response does not include provider names, endpoints, or API keys.
Admins can check redacted readiness counts with GET /v1.0/configuration/external-search/status
queries.answer: A redacted external-search readiness summary without provider names, endpoints or API keys.

queries.text: What does the ExposeDocumentSourceUrls assistant setting control?
evidence: SourceUrl is only populated when the assistant setting ExposeDocumentSourceUrls is enabled.
queries.answer: Whether SourceUrl is included in attached-document metadata.

queries.text: What does chat_history.origin record?
evidence: chat_history.origin now records request source such as web or slack
Origin of the chat request (e.g. web, slack, api).
queries.answer: The source of the chat request, such as web, slack or api.

queries.text: What does the X-Thread-ID header do on a chat request?
evidence: When provided, the server records timing metrics and conversation history for this turn.
History entries are created automatically when the X-Thread-ID header is provided on chat requests.
queries.answer: It ties the request to a thread so timing metrics and chat history are recorded for the turn.

queries.text: Which version of the EasySlack package does AssistantHub use?
evidence: AssistantHub consumes the EasySlack NuGet package at version 1.0.1
Consume EasySlack as a NuGet package at version 1.0.1
queries.answer: EasySlack 1.0.1 from NuGet.

queries.text: Which values does ASSISTANTHUB_TEST_SUITES accept?
evidence: Supported values: model, service, api, integration, mcp.
queries.answer: model, service, api, integration and mcp.

queries.text: What does Verbex.RequireIngestion do?
evidence: When true, document ingestion fails if Verbex indexing fails. When false, failures are logged and ingestion continues.
queries.answer: If true (default), a Verbex indexing failure fails ingestion; if false it is logged and ingestion continues.

queries.text: What does the LoadModelsOnChatOpen setting do?
evidence: Load or warm configured completion and embedding endpoint models when a chat window opens.
queries.answer: Loads or warms the assistant's completion and embedding models when a chat window opens (default false).

queries.text: What prefix do AssistantHub tenant IDs use?
evidence: Use k-sortable IDs with ten_ prefix (consistent with RecallDB/Partio/Verbex)
queries.answer: ten_ (k-sortable IDs).

queries.text: What schema changes are in migrations/003_upgrade_to_v0.5.0.sql?
evidence: v0.5.0 includes schema changes to add crawl_plans and crawl_operations tables and add crawl_plan_id, crawl_operation_id, source_url columns to assistant_documents
queries.answer: Adds crawl_plans and crawl_operations tables and crawl_plan_id, crawl_operation_id, source_url columns on assistant_documents.

queries.text: What is the default for ReturnFullSearchContent?
evidence: ReturnFullSearchContent stays false by default so search returns excerpts and exact text is requested through collection_read_chunks
When false, collection_search returns excerpts and ContentOmitted=true
queries.answer: false: collection_search returns excerpts and full text is read via collection_read_chunks.

queries.text: What is the default Telemetry SamplingRatio?
evidence: Head-based sampling is configurable (SamplingRatio, default 1.0 = sample everything) via a parent-based sampler
queries.answer: 1.0 (sample everything).

queries.text: What does IsProtected = true mean for a tenant, user or credential?
evidence: Default tenant, admin user, and credential are marked IsProtected = true and cannot be deleted via API (returns 403).
Deactivate protected records by setting Active = false instead
queries.answer: The record can't be deleted through the API (403); deactivate it with Active = false instead.

queries.text: I'm monitoring the MCP server: what's its default HTTP JSON-RPC endpoint, and which Prometheus metric counts its tool calls?
evidence: HTTP JSON-RPC http://127.0.0.1:8820/rpc Voltaic HTTP transport
mcp.server.tool.calls Counter {call} mcp.tool, mcp.transport, outcome mcp_server_tool_calls_total
queries.answer: http://127.0.0.1:8820/rpc; mcp_server_tool_calls_total.

queries.text: Which local URLs do I open in a browser for the AssistantHub dashboard and for Grafana?
evidence: The AssistantHub dashboard server URL should be set to http://localhost:8801
Open Grafana at http://localhost:3000 (admin/admin) and browse the AssistantHub folder.
queries.answer: http://localhost:8801 for AssistantHub and http://localhost:3000 for Grafana.

queries.text: What are the default logins for the AssistantHub dashboard and for Grafana?
evidence: Email admin@assistanthub Password password
Grafana assistanthub-grafana 3000 admin / admin
queries.answer: AssistantHub: admin@assistanthub / password; Grafana: admin / admin.

queries.text: What's the Verbex admin API key in the default Docker setup, and which setting caps how much text gets sent to Verbex per document?
evidence: Admin API Key verbexadmin
Optional maximum normalized text characters sent to Verbex per document record. 0 means unlimited.
queries.answer: verbexadmin; Verbex.MaxContentCharacters (0 = unlimited).

queries.text: Which chat request field restricts retrieval to specific documents, and which MCP tool lists the documents a user can pick?
evidence: When present, RAG retrieval is constrained to those completed documents in the assistant's configured collection.
Assistant public document listing is exposed as assistant/documents/list and mirrors GET /v1.0/assistants/{assistantId}/documents.
queries.answer: attached_document_ids; the MCP tool assistant/documents/list.

queries.text: How do I backfill existing documents into Verbex over REST after upgrading, and what's the equivalent MCP tool?
evidence: Existing completed documents from deployments upgraded to v0.14.0 need a one-time admin reindex before they appear in ARTIFACTS > Indices > Search.
Reindex a page of completed documents into Verbex
Reindex a bounded page of completed documents into Verbex for upgrade/backfill and repair workflows.
queries.answer: POST /v1.0/documents/reindex (or /v1.0/documents/{id}/reindex); in MCP use document/reindex-batch or document/reindex.

queries.text: The old design notes say query rewrite and re-ranking reuse the main inference endpoint. Is that still how it works, and when did it change?
evidence: Re-ranking uses the same resolved inference endpoint as the retrieval gate, query rewrite, and final completion.
Retrieval gate, query rewrite, and re-ranking now honor their dedicated endpoint settings while falling back to InferenceEndpointId when unset.
queries.answer: Not necessarily: since v0.11.0 they can use dedicated endpoints (QueryRewriteInferenceEndpointId, RerankInferenceEndpointId), falling back to InferenceEndpointId.

queries.text: Which operation domains does the telemetry duration metric use, and which stage names can show up in a chat turn's PerformanceJson?
evidence: Domains: inference, retrieval, ingestion, storage, vector, index, object, crawl, eval, auth, chat, embedding, chunking.
Known stage names include retrieval_gate, query_rewrite, retrieval, rerank, endpoint_resolution, context_compaction, tools, and final_inference.
queries.answer: Domains: inference, retrieval, ingestion, storage, vector, index, object, crawl, eval, auth, chat, embedding, chunking. Stages: retrieval_gate, query_rewrite, retrieval, rerank, endpoint_resolution, context_compaction, tools, final_inference.

queries.text: What .NET SDK do I need to run the MCP server, and which .NET version does the C# client SDK target?
evidence: .NET 10 SDK
.NET 8.0, System.Text.Json, typed exceptions, IAsyncEnumerable streaming
queries.answer: .NET 10 SDK for the MCP server; the C# SDK targets .NET 8.0.

queries.text: Which release added NFS crawling, and which NFS settings have to line up with the export policy?
evidence: v0.16.0 adds CIFS and NFS file-server crawler support alongside the existing web crawler
verify the AssistantHub server or container can resolve and reach the export, and that NfsUserId, NfsGroupId, and NfsVersion match the export policy
queries.answer: v0.16.0; NfsUserId, NfsGroupId and NfsVersion must match the export policy.

queries.text: Which Prometheus metric tracks REST request latency, and which API gives me per-assistant p95/p99 latency?
evidence: http.server.request.duration Histogram s http.request.method, http.route, http.response.status_code
Response fields include: RequestCount, SuccessCount, FailureCount, SuccessRate, AverageDurationMs, P50DurationMs, P90DurationMs, P95DurationMs, P99DurationMs
queries.answer: http_server_request_duration_seconds (http.server.request.duration); GET /v1.0/assistants/{assistantId}/analytics/overview.

queries.text: How long are assistant tool-call traces retained, and which MCP tools let me list or delete them?
evidence: Tool-call trace retention follows RequestHistory.RetentionDays.
assistant/tool-calls/list, assistant/tool-calls/get, assistant/tool-calls/delete, assistant/tool-calls/delete-bulk
queries.answer: They follow RequestHistory.RetentionDays; MCP tools assistant/tool-calls/list, get, delete and delete-bulk.

queries.text: Can I open the Swagger UI through the MCP server, and where is it served over REST?
evidence: Browser Swagger UI; use system/openapi for the OpenAPI JSON from MCP
Serves the Swagger UI for the live AssistantHub OpenAPI document.
Swagger rendering at http://localhost:8800/swagger
queries.answer: No, it's deferred in MCP (use system/openapi); over REST it's GET /swagger, e.g. http://localhost:8800/swagger.

queries.text: What prefix must the Slack bot token have, and will the MCP server show that token when I fetch assistant settings?
evidence: SlackBotToken must start with xoxb-
assistant/settings/get and assistant/settings/update return redacted secret-bearing fields by default.
queries.answer: It must start with xoxb-; MCP redacts it unless includeSecrets=true.

queries.text: Which archived plans introduced the chat_history origin column and the chat_history metadata_filter column?
evidence: Also add origin to chat_history across all supported DB providers and CRUD paths.
Add column metadata_filter TEXT to chat_history CREATE TABLE
queries.answer: The Slack Integration plan added origin; the Metadata Filtering plan added metadata_filter.

queries.text: Is there a cap on how many time buckets an assistant analytics query returns?
evidence: Optional bucket width. The server caps responses to 240 buckets.
queries.answer: Yes, 240 buckets.

queries.text: What's the largest limit I can pass to the assistant analytics slowest-requests endpoint?
evidence: Returns the slowest request-history rows in the selected range
and limit (default 25, max 250)
queries.answer: 250 (default 25).

queries.text: How big can the files users attach from their own computer to a chat be?
evidence: Per-file uploads are limited to 10 MB, the total local upload payload is limited to 25 MB
queries.answer: 10 MB per file and 25 MB total per request.

queries.text: If I PUT the configuration back with the Tavily API key still showing as REDACTED, will it wipe my real key?
evidence: If a previously returned ExternalSearch.Providers.ApiKey value is submitted as REDACTED, the existing configured provider key is preserved.
queries.answer: No, the existing provider key is preserved.

queries.text: When I create a Verbex index record through AssistantHub without a Name, what does it get filled with?
evidence: If Name is omitted or blank, AssistantHub populates it from ObjectName, CustomMetadata.ObjectName, object key/source URL basename, Id/Identifier, or record
queries.answer: The first available of ObjectName, CustomMetadata.ObjectName, object key/source URL basename, Id/Identifier, or 'record'.

queries.text: Does the tool-policy dry-run diagnostics route actually call the model or execute any tools?
evidence: Run administrator dry-run diagnostics for a draft assistant tool policy without saving it, calling the model, or executing tools.
queries.answer: No. It validates the draft policy and endpoint metadata without saving, calling the model, or executing tools.

queries.text: When a crawl plan connectivity test can't reach the share, what HTTP status does the API return?
evidence: Validation errors return 400 Bad Request. A failed repository connection returns 200 OK with Success=false.
queries.answer: 200 OK with Success=false (400 is only for validation errors).

queries.text: What happens on a tool-enabled chat if the routing endpoint doesn't advertise tool-calling support?
evidence: If capability is missing, the server returns a configuration error before calling the model.
queries.answer: The server returns a configuration error before calling the model.

queries.text: What max_connections does the Docker PostgreSQL run with, and why?
evidence: so concurrent document ingestion, Verbex indexing, RecallDB embedding writes, object storage, and dashboard/API activity have enough connection headroom during crawler bursts
queries.answer: 250, to give ingestion, indexing, storage and dashboard/API traffic connection headroom during crawler bursts.

queries.text: I'm on Linux without Docker Desktop. What address should AssistantHub use to reach Ollama running on the host?
evidence: Use http://172.17.0.1:11434 (the default Docker bridge gateway), or run the compose stack with network_mode: host.
queries.answer: http://172.17.0.1:11434 (the Docker bridge gateway), or use network_mode: host.

queries.text: After pointing Partio at my own Ollama, endpoint health checks fail with an invalid request URI error. What's wrong?
evidence: Change the Health Check URL from a relative path (/api/tags) to a fully-qualified URL
Health checks using relative paths will fail with an "invalid request URI" error.
queries.answer: The health check URL is relative; change /api/tags to a fully-qualified URL.

queries.text: When a tenant is deleted, are its Verbex indices cleaned up as well?
evidence: Delete a tenant and deprovision all associated resources (users, credentials, assistants, documents, S3 buckets, RecallDB tenant, and mapped Verbex tenant/index resources).
queries.answer: Yes, mapped Verbex tenant/index resources are deprovisioned too.

queries.text: Where does AssistantHub keep the Verbex tenant ID and default index ID for tenants other than the default one?
evidence: AssistantHub stores the generated Verbex tenant ID and deterministic default index ID in tenant tags (VerbexTenantId, VerbexDefaultIndexId) during provisioning.
queries.answer: In tenant tags VerbexTenantId and VerbexDefaultIndexId.

queries.text: What does the compact endpoint give back, and what should my chat client do with it?
evidence: The generated summary is returned as a system message; clients should retain it for the next chat request and may hide it from the visible transcript.
queries.answer: A system-message summary; keep it for the next chat request (it can be hidden from the transcript).

queries.text: Does the batch reindex route re-process documents that already have a Verbex record?
evidence: Batch mode skips non-completed documents and, by default, skips documents that already have VerbexRecordId.
Set IncludeAlreadyIndexed to true to repair or replace existing Verbex records.
queries.answer: Not by default; set IncludeAlreadyIndexed to true to reindex them.

queries.text: What port does the Verbex dashboard container use?
evidence: verbex-dashboard 8502 Web-based management UI for Verbex.

queries.text: What's the Prometheus name of the counter for ingested documents?
evidence: ingestion.documents Counter {document} outcome ingestion_documents_total
queries.answer: ingestion_documents_total (labelled by outcome).
